html.<b>El reto.</b> Una aplicación clínica t: The challenge. A clinical application had to receive patient data from three hospitals that store it differently (HL7 v2.3, FHIR and Excel), without writing an integration for each one.
html.<b>Así se vería la instalación.</b> Mult: What the installation would look like. Multi Bridge is installed locally, on a computer in one hospital: it reads that hospital's files there, and patient data never leaves its network. This panel is what that team would see: its connections to the application and the recipes it has already approved. Here the three challenge hospitals are shown together.
html.<b>Cómo se conecta un hospital.</b> Puls: How a hospital gets connected. Click one: Multi Bridge proposes which data each field comes from, a person reviews it and approves it with their name, and that recipe is reused automatically the next time a file like it arrives.
html.Cómo quieres recibir los datos. Elige un: How you want to receive the data. Pick one to see it, or create your own in three ways: with all the fields of a file (the same data, in another format), field by field, or by uploading an example of the output.
html.De dos maneras. Con una <b>lista de camp: In two ways. With a field list: the format (JSON, CSV, Excel or XML) and the name and type of each field; it is created here and saved in expected/<name>.fields.json, with names and types only. Or with an example of how you want the data, in its own format (FHIR too: expected/<name>.example.<ext>), plus optional rules an example can't show: what is required, allowed values, units, which field to group by (expected/<name>.rules.json); the output is written like the example. If you change a format, the recipes approved for the previous version stop applying automatically and must be reviewed again.
html.…o elige solo el formato, sin ejemplo. C: …or just pick the format, with no example. With the box ticked you receive every column of the source file in that format, with its name and type; then you can remove the ones you don't want and save it for next time:
html.Demo: todo se ejecuta en tu navegador y: Demo: everything runs in your browser and your files never leave your computer. Rules only; for the local AI, install it on your computer.
